cast.theme: Weekly meeting of a university ecology research lab

personas.name: Odile
personas.goals: A smooth move and a productive summer
personas.hidden_agenda: Writing the grant renewal and anxious about it

personas.name: Sanjay
personas.hidden_agenda: Wants a site in the mountains that is a long drive away

personas.name: Bryn
personas.goals: Get the first paper through review
personas.hidden_agenda: Reviewer two has been harsh and Bryn is discouraged

personas.name: Lottie
personas.role: Lab coordinator, runs the undergraduate program
personas.goals: A good summer for the undergrads
personas.hidden_agenda: Has been promised a bigger budget than the grant has

agenda.title: Summer bee surveys
agenda.goal: Finalize sites and traps for the season

agenda.title: The lab move
agenda.goal: Plan the move to the new building

agenda.title: Papers
agenda.goal: Status of the two papers under review

beats.summary: Sites and traps; Sanjay's site count is high
The summer program; Lottie's headcount stands

turns.speaker: Odile
turns.text: Good morning. Surveys first, since the season starts soon. Sanjay?

turns.speaker: Sanjay
turns.text: We'll survey about thirty sites this summer, same as last year.

turns.speaker: Lottie
turns.text: I have twenty-two on the permit list. Did we add some?

turns.speaker: Sanjay
turns.text: No, you're right, twenty-two. I was thinking of the sites we scouted, not the ones we kept.

turns.speaker: Odile
turns.text: Twenty-two is plenty. How many traps?

turns.speaker: Sanjay
turns.text: A hundred and forty pan traps. Most of them survived the winter in the shed.

turns.speaker: Bryn
turns.text: The species count is up to eighty-seven, by the way. Two new ones from the meadow site last week.

turns.speaker: Odile
turns.text: Eighty-seven. That's wonderful.

turns.speaker: Sanjay
turns.text: I'd still love to add a mountain site. The bees up there are completely different.

turns.speaker: Odile
turns.text: How far is the mountain site?

turns.speaker: Sanjay
turns.text: About three hours each way.

turns.speaker: Lottie
turns.text: That's a full day of driving for one site.

turns.speaker: Sanjay
turns.text: Could we drop a couple of the meadow sites to make room for it?

turns.speaker: Odile
turns.text: Let's leave the mountain site for next year, when we have the new grant.

turns.speaker: Sanjay
turns.text: Fair. I'll scout it on a weekend anyway, out of curiosity.

turns.speaker: Bryn
turns.text: The meadow farmer asked if we could share our species list with him. He's very proud of his bees.

turns.speaker: Odile
turns.text: Of course. I'll send him a copy with a thank-you note.

turns.speaker: Bryn
turns.text: He'll love that.

turns.speaker: Odile
turns.text: The move. We go to the new building on August fifteenth.

turns.speaker: Lottie
turns.text: That's right in the middle of the field season.

turns.speaker: Odile
turns.text: I know. The university picked the date.

turns.speaker: Bryn
turns.text: What happens to the specimens?

turns.speaker: Sanjay
turns.text: Forty-six hundred pinned specimens, in drawers. They move as they are, carefully.

turns.speaker: Lottie
turns.text: And three freezers. Those need a proper moving company.

turns.speaker: Odile
turns.text: Then the freezers go with the university's movers and the specimens go with us, by hand.

turns.speaker: Bryn
turns.text: Are there greenhouse bays in the new building?

turns.speaker: Odile
turns.text: Four. More than we have now.

turns.speaker: Sanjay
turns.text: Four bays. We could finally run the nesting experiment.

turns.speaker: Lottie
turns.text: My cousin moved labs last year and they lost a whole freezer of samples because the power was off for an hour.

turns.speaker: Bryn
turns.text: That's my nightmare. Literally, I've had that dream.

turns.speaker: Odile
turns.text: Let's not lose any freezers. Lottie, could you ask facilities about backup power for the move day?

turns.speaker: Lottie
turns.text: I'll email facilities this afternoon.

turns.speaker: Odile
turns.text: Papers. Two are under review.

turns.speaker: Bryn
turns.text: Mine came back from reviewer two. They want a whole new analysis.

turns.speaker: Odile
turns.text: How big a change?

turns.speaker: Bryn
turns.text: A few weeks of work, if I do it properly. I'm a bit discouraged, honestly.

turns.speaker: Odile
turns.text: That's normal. The analysis they asked for is fair. It'll make the paper better.

turns.speaker: Sanjay
turns.text: I can help with the model. I did something similar last year.

turns.speaker: Bryn
turns.text: Thank you. That helps more than you know.

turns.speaker: Odile
turns.text: The other paper is still waiting for the editor.

turns.speaker: Lottie
turns.text: Undergrads. We have eight starting in June.

turns.speaker: Odile
turns.text: At fifteen dollars an hour?

turns.speaker: Lottie
turns.text: Fifteen, yes. The department raised it last year.

turns.speaker: Sanjay
turns.text: Eight is great for the surveys. Two per vehicle.

turns.speaker: Bryn
turns.text: Could they each get a small project of their own, not just trap duty?

turns.speaker: Odile
turns.text: Yes. Pick something they can present at the regional conference on October second.

turns.speaker: Lottie
turns.text: I'll draft a list of small projects and share it before June.

turns.speaker: Sanjay
turns.text: Somebody will need to do safety training with them on the first day.

turns.speaker: Odile
turns.text: When does the grant end, again? I want to make sure the summer pay is covered.

turns.speaker: Lottie
turns.text: December thirty-first. The summer is covered.

turns.speaker: Bryn
turns.text: Will the new building have parking for the field vehicles?

turns.speaker: Odile
turns.text: Thank you, everyone. A good week. Let's have a good summer.
